directive:
Apply only the tied-cutoff repair; preserve every causal assumption, definition, lemma, theorem, converse, witness, and finite-sample coverage claim.

Fix once and for all a single-valued ordered Gram-spectral selector: for every H, it selects an orthonormal eigenbasis of HH^T ordered by nonincreasing eigenvalue and includes a fixed choice within every tied eigenspace. This may be a classical noncomputable choice, matching the Lean helper. Define the selected projection P*_{r0}(H) onto its first r0 vectors, H*_{r0}=P*_{r0}(H)H, and phi_{r0}(H,z,b)=z^T(H*_{r0})^dagger b. Thus phi is a genuine scalar function even at a tied cutoff; do not replace it by a set-valued functional.

Let q=min(m,|E|) and adopt sigma_{q+1}(H)=0. State that when sigma_{r0}(H)>sigma_{r0+1}(H), the retained subspace and phi are independent of the selector. Define the population delta-method variance only on this gap-separated differentiability region. Define the plug-in variance by the ordinary derivative there and by one fixed nonnegative fallback, such as 0, when the empirical cutoff gap fails. Keep the Wald-estimator and Wald-interval formulas unchanged, adding only mechanically necessary wording that they use this selector-based phi and totalized variance.

In oeq:studentized-uniform-projection, retain the existing coverage, diameter, and Hausdorff requirements. Clarify that rank(Hx)=r0 and sigma_{r0}(Hx)>=c imply sigma_{r0+1}(Hx)=0 and a strict cutoff gap; consequently, for each fixed regular M, the selector and fallback are asymptotically inactive. Do not strengthen the open question or change its admissible array class.

Make substantive edits only to the five required targets. Do not add assumptions or alter any causal claim.

changed.from: \(\widehat V_n\) is the plug-in delta-method variance for \(\phi_{r_0}(\widehat H_{x,n},\widehat z_{x,y,n},\widehat b_n)\), using the joint source multinomial covariance and target multinomial covariance with allocation factors \(p^{-1}\) and \((1-p)^{-1}\).
changed.to:
Put \(\widehat T_n=(\widehat H_{x,n},\widehat z_{x,y,n},\widehat b_n)\), and let \(\widehat\Gamma_n\) be the plug-in covariance matrix of \(\sqrt n\,\widehat T_n\), formed from the joint source multinomial covariance and the target multinomial covariance with allocation factors \(p^{-1}\) and \((1-p)^{-1}\). The totalized plug-in variance is
\[
\widehat V_n=
\begin{cases}
D\phi_{r_0}(\widehat T_n)\,\widehat\Gamma_n\,D\phi_{r_0}(\widehat T_n)^{\top},
&\sigma_{r_0}(\widehat H_{x,n})>\sigma_{r_0+1}(\widehat H_{x,n}),\\
0,&\sigma_{r_0}(\widehat H_{x,n})\le\sigma_{r_0+1}(\widehat H_{x,n}),
\end{cases}
\]
where \(D\phi_{r_0}\) is the ordinary derivative of the selector-independent functional on the strict-cutoff-gap region and \(\sigma_{\bar q+1}=0\) for \(\bar q=\min(m,\lvert\mathcal E\rvert)\). The second line is the fixed nonnegative fallback.
changed.reason: The plug-in variance must be totalized because the ordinary derivative is defined only on the strict-cutoff-gap region. The proposed construction uses that derivative on the region and the fixed nonnegative fallback zero otherwise.
